title: U.S. House, District 20
what_it_does: Represents Florida's 20th Congressional District in the U.S. House of Representatives; votes on federal laws and spending.
verified_ballot_note: Regular (full-term) election for the newly drawn CD 20. Roster from CBS Miami and WLRN: Debbie Wasserman Schultz (D) will face Republican nominee Brent Andersen and NPA candidate Kedner Maxime; Kevin McClellan filed as a write-in. The seat itself has been vacant since Rep. Sheila Cherfilus-McCormick resigned Apr. 21, 2026; a separate special election for the remainder of the term (under the old lines) was also scheduled with an Aug. 18 primary and Nov. 3 general, and its ballot could not be verified here, so voters in the old CD 20 may see two CD 20 contests. County makeup for the new district was not confirmed. Sources: https://www.cbsnews.com/miami/news/2026-florida-primary-district-20-democratic-debbie-wasserman-schultz/ ; https://www.wlrn.org/government-politics/2026-08-18/wasserman-schultz-wins-fla-s-20th-district-amid-outcry-over-black-representation-in-south-florida ; https://news.ballotpedia.org/2026/04/22/sheila-cherfilus-mccormicks-resignation-leaves-floridas-20th-congressional-district-vacant/ Florida adopted a new congressional map (passed Apr 29, 2026, signed May 4, 2026) that reworked 21 of 28 districts; county descriptions here reflect post-redistricting reporting where found (https://www.wusf.org/politics-issues/2026-05-06/breakdown-changes-for-florida-new-congressional-map).

candidates.name: Debbie Wasserman Schultz
candidates.photo_source: congress.gov member portrait (bioguide ID from memory, unverified)
candidates.background: Debbie Wasserman Schultz has served in the U.S. House since 2005 and currently represents Florida's 25th District; after the 2026 map moved her home out of that district she ran in the new 20th. She won the Aug. 18, 2026 Democratic primary with about 45% (more than 30,000 votes), defeating former Broward Mayor Dale Holness (about 23%), former Rep. Sheila Cherfilus-McCormick, teacher Elijah Manley and Luther Campbell. Note: she is a sitting member of Congress but not the incumbent for the CD 20 seat, which is vacant.
candidates.primary_result: Won Aug 18, 2026 Democratic primary with ~45% over Holness (~23%), Cherfilus-McCormick, Manley and Campbell (CBS Miami; WLRN)
